claims.claim: Two placebo-controlled trials found oral collagen peptides increased skin hydration after 8 weeks, and increased dermal collagen density while decreasing fragmentation after 4 weeks, with effects persisting at 12 weeks.
claims.episode_span: oral collagen peptide supplementation increased skin hydration after 8 weeks
claims.source_title: The effect of oral collagen peptide supplementation on skin moisture and the dermal collagen network
claims.supporting_quote: Oral collagen peptide supplementation significantly increased skin hydration after 8 weeks of intake. The collagen density in the dermis significantly increased and the fragmentation of the dermal collagen network significantly decreased already after 4 weeks of supplementation. Both effects persisted after 12 weeks.

claims.claim: Ex vivo human skin explants showed collagen peptides induce collagen and glycosaminoglycan production.
claims.episode_span: collagen peptides induced collagen and glycosaminoglycan production
claims.source_title: The effect of oral collagen peptide supplementation on skin moisture and the dermal collagen network
claims.supporting_quote: Ex vivo experiments demonstrated that collagen peptides induce collagen as well as glycosaminoglycan production, offering a mechanistic explanation for the observed clinical effects.

claims.claim: A randomized placebo-controlled trial in Korean adults aged 19 to 60 with damaged hair and without alopecia found 24 weeks of LMWCP GT improved hair gloss, elasticity, and scalp elasticity versus placebo, with no treatment-related adverse events.
claims.episode_span: significant improvements in hair gloss, measured with a gloss meter and scanning electron microscopy, and in hair elasticity
claims.source_title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Molecular-Weight Collagen Peptide GT for Improving Hair Condition
claims.supporting_quote: Compared with placebo, the treatment group demonstrated significant improvements in hair gloss, as measured using a gloss meter (SAMBA) and scanning electron microscopy, as well as in hair elasticity, assessed by tensile strength and hair diameter.

claims.claim: In 22 premenopausal female distance runners, four weeks of collagen peptide supplementation increased P1NP versus placebo (interaction p = 0.04) and showed an IL-6 interaction (p = 0.03), with no significant CTX-1 interaction (p = 0.13).
claims.episode_span: A group-by-time interaction for P1NP, a marker of bone formation, was significant at p = 0.04
claims.source_title: Effects of collagen peptide supplementation on bone turnover, cytokine, and inflammatory markers in female distance runners
claims.supporting_quote: A significant group × time interaction was observed for P1NP ( p  = 0.04), with increases in INT and no change in CON. No significant interaction was observed for CTX-1 ( p  = 0.13).

claims.claim: Among 53 men with sarcopenia, mean age 72.2 years, collagen peptides plus 12 weeks of resistance training improved fat-free mass, quadriceps strength, and fat loss more than training plus placebo.
claims.episode_span: fat-free mass +4.2 kg (standard deviation 2.31) versus +2.9 kg (standard deviation 1.84)
claims.source_title: Collagen peptide supplementation in combination with resistance training improves body composition and increases muscle strength in elderly sarcopenic men
claims.supporting_quote: The effect was significantly more pronounced in subjects receiving collagen peptides: FFM (TG +4·2 (sd 2·31) kg/PG +2·9 (sd 1·84) kg; P<0·05); IQS (TG +16·5 (sd 12·9) Nm/PG +7·3 (sd 13·2) Nm; P<0·05); and FM (TG -5·4 (sd 3·17) kg/PG -3·5 (sd 2·16) kg; P<0·05).
